title: FaaSGraph: Enabling Scalable, Efficient, and Cost-Effective Graph Processing with Serverless Computing
problem: Graph processing frameworks deployed on Infrastructure-as-a-Service models suffer from limited elasticity and inefficient resource utilization. Current approaches fail to leverage serverless computing's elasticity for dynamic graph workloads.
motivation: Graph processing is critical for cloud services, but current IaaS-based approaches are inefficient and costly, limiting adoption.
method: FaaSGraph co-designs a graph processing framework with serverless computing by making data flow—not computation scheduling—the primary design concern. Instead of fitting traditional graph algorithms into serverless functions (which have limited memory, short run times, and execute across many machines in parallel), it restructures the graph algorithms themselves to match these constraints. By carefully organizing data movement between functions and optimizing for computation-heavy workloads, it reduces the overhead that normally makes serverless graph processing inefficient.
key_novelty: The innovation is a serverless execution model centered on data flow—rather than computation scheduling—that enables efficient graph processing by restructuring algorithms to work within serverless constraints (limited memory and runtime per function) while automatically scaling with demand.
contributions: Data-centric serverless execution model optimized for compute-intensive graph workloads
Graph processing paradigm co-designed with serverless computing model
8.3X end-to-end performance improvement and 52.4% memory reduction versus IaaS methods
85.7% cost reduction with steady 99-percentile performance under fluctuating workloads
